mainTopic: Where and how the burned offerings are burned, then the new פרק on slaughtering and offering up outside the עזרה and the source for its warning.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a derivation that the burned bulls and goats are burned east of ירושלים. It then asks where the רבנן burn them. A ברייתא answers: north of ירושלים, outside the three camps, while רבי יוסי הגלילי requires the בית הדשן. רבא says רבי אליעזר בן יעקב disagrees with him, because he reads 'שפך הדשן' as a sloped place. אביי replies that maybe he requires both ashes and a slope. A ברייתא then teaches that only someone who helps during the actual burning makes his clothes טמא, and that this stops once the animals become ash. רבי שמעון says it stops once the flesh is burned away, and רבא explains that the two views differ over a charred lump. Then פרק טבול יום ends, and a new משנה rules that one who slaughters and offers up a קרבן outside is liable for each act, with רבי יוסי הגלילי disagreeing. The parallel case of a טמא person eating קדשים follows. The גמרא then searches for the אזהרה against slaughtering outside. It finds ״ולא יזבחו עוד״, defends it with רבה's double reading, and begins a new challenge from a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: So too here: east of ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: The derivation that began earlier ends. Just as in the other case the place outside the camp is to the east, these burned offerings are burned east of ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too here, they are burned east of ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a comparison that started before this section. The result is that the burned bulls and goats are burned on the east side of ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the end of a learning-out that compares one case of 'outside the camp' to another. Whatever direction applies there applies here too, so the answer is east. This is one opinion, and the next step asks what the other side holds.

keyTerms.meaning: So too here. This phrase finishes a comparison: what is true there is true here.
East
Jerusalem

phrases.english: so too here – to the east of Jerusalem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends a derivation that began in the earlier text.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: By this view, the burned offerings are burned east of ירושלים.

steps.title: Where do the רבנן burn them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the רבנן, who disagree with the view just stated, would burn these offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the רבנן, where do they burn them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question: if the רבנן do not say 'east,' which direction do they say? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just heard one opinion, east of ירושלים. The word אלא signals a switch to the opposing side, and the גמרא wants to know their location.

keyTerms.meaning: But. Here it switches to the other opinion.
The Rabbis, meaning the majority opinion
Where?
Burns

phrases.english: But according to the Rabbis,
where does one burn them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the 'east' opinion to ask about the opposing רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The location where the רבנן would burn the פרים ושעירים הנשרפים.

steps.title: A ברייתא: north of ירושלים, or on the ash pile
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא answers: north of ירושלים, outside the three camps. רבי יוסי הגלילי says they are burned on the בית הדשן.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: Where are they burned? North of ירושלים, outside the three camps. רבי יוסי הגלילי says: they are burned on the בית הדשן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a ברייתא. The רבנן say the burning is north of ירושלים, outside the three camps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we have the direction for the רבנן: north. The ברייתא also brings a second opinion. רבי יוסי הגלילי requires the burning to be on the specific spot where the ashes are dumped, the בית הדשן. That opinion becomes the focus of the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: North
The three camps
The place where the ashes are dumped

phrases.english: As it is taught: Where are they burned?
To the north of Jerusalem,
outside the three camps.
phrases.notes: The three camps are the areas of the שכינה, the לויים, and ישראל. The burning has to be beyond all of them.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
They are burned on the place of the ashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן say north of ירושלים, outside the three camps. רבי יוסי הגלילי adds that it must be on the בית הדשן.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two locations to keep in mind: north of ירושלים outside the three camps (the רבנן), and on the בית הדשן (רבי יוסי הגלילי).

steps.title: רבא identifies who disagrees with רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks which תנא disagrees with רבי יוסי הגלילי and answers that it is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Who is the תנא who disagrees with רבי יוסי הגלילי? It is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא names the תנא who does not require burning on the בית הדשן. He says it is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and the next step brings his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone must hold that the burning does not have to be on the ash pile. רבא claims it is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. He will support this from a ברייתא about how to read the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא?
Who disagrees with him

phrases.english: Rava said: Who is the tanna
who disagrees with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili?
It is Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תַּנָּא דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי יוסי הגלילי's opinion and looks for the opposing תנא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is the תנא who disagrees with רבי יוסי הגלילי and does not require the בית הדשן.

steps.title: The ברייתא on 'where the ashes are poured'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא on 'על שפך הדשן ישרף' has two readings. The תנא קמא says ashes must be there. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says the place must be sloped.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'On the pouring of the ashes it shall be burned' means ashes should be there. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says it means its place should be sloped.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings his proof. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads the words 'שפך הדשן' as describing a sloping place, not a place of ashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא reads 'שפך הדשן' as 'where ashes are,' which matches רבי יוסי הגלילי. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads 'שפך' as 'sloped.' רבא concludes that he no longer needs the ash place, so he disagrees with רבי יוסי הגלילי.

keyTerms.meaning: The pouring of the ashes (ויקרא 4:12)
Sloped, so things slide down
Its place

phrases.english: as it is taught: “On the pouring of the ashes it shall be burned” –
that there should be ashes there
(that ashes should be brought there first).
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
that its place should be sloped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רבא's identification in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב disagrees with רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads 'שפך הדשן' as 'a sloped place' rather than 'a place of ashes.'

steps.title: אביי: maybe they only argue about the slope
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. Perhaps רבי אליעזר בן יעקב agrees that ashes must be there, and the argument is only whether the place must also be sloped.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Perhaps they argue only about whether its place must be sloped.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבא's proof. The ברייתא might not show that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב drops the ash place at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא assumed that if the פסוק teaches 'sloped,' it no longer teaches 'ashes.' אביי suggests a different picture: everyone agrees on the ash place, and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב only adds a slope requirement. If so, he does not disagree with רבי יוסי הגלילי, and the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps. It opens a rejection.
They disagree

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying רבי אליעזר בן יעקב drops the slope. He means רבי אליעזר בן יעקב may require both ashes and a slope, while the תנא קמא requires only ashes.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Perhaps they disagree about whether its place must be sloped.
phrases.notes: He means only that. Both sides may still agree it must be the place of the ashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 5 for רבא's claim in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only. It does not show that רבא's identification is wrong.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may show only an added slope requirement, not that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב drops the ash place.

steps.title: Only the one who actually burns becomes impure
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that only the person who helps during the actual burning makes his clothes טמא. The person who lights the fire or arranges the wood does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: The one who burns makes his clothes impure. The one who lights the fire does not make his clothes impure, and the one who sets up the woodpile does not make his clothes impure. Who counts as 'the one who burns'? Someone who helps at the time of the burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that explains exactly which person becomes טמא through burning the פר and שעיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the one who burns them must wash his clothes. The ברייתא reads this narrowly: lighting the fire or arranging the wood is only preparation and is not 'burning.' Only someone who helps while the animals are actually being burned falls under this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who burns
Makes his clothes ritually impure
The one who kindles or lights the fire
The arranged pile of wood for the fire
The one who helps or assists

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that everyone involved in the burning becomes טמא. Only the person helping during the actual burning does.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The one who burns renders his garments impure,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הַמַּצִּית אֶת הָאוּר מְטַמֵּא בְּגָדִים,
phrases.english: but the one who kindles the fire does not render his garments impure,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הַמְסַדֵּר אֶת הַמַּעֲרָכָה מְטַמֵּא בְּגָדִים.
phrases.english: and the one who arranges the woodpile does not render his garments impure.
And who is the one who burns?
One who assists at the time of the burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where the burned offerings are burned to who becomes טמא by burning them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only one who assists during the actual burning makes his clothes טמא. The one who lights the fire or arranges the wood does not.

steps.title: Impurity stops once the animals turn to ash
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא learns from the word 'אותם' that once the animals become ash, they no longer make clothes טמא. רבי שמעון says the טומאה stops as soon as the flesh is burned away.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think he makes his clothes impure even after they have become ash. So the verse says 'them': they make clothes impure, but once they become ash they do not. רבי שמעון says: 'them' make clothes impure, but once the flesh has been burned away, they do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and asks how long the animals keep causing טומאה. The תנא קמא and רבי שמעון each give a different cut-off point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אותם' teaches that the טומאה applies only while the animals are still recognizably 'them.' The תנא קמא says this lasts until they become actual ash. רבי שמעון says it ends earlier, once the flesh has been burned away.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought. This introduces a wrong assumption.
The verse teaches. This introduces the proof from the פסוק.
Them. The key word in the פסוק.
Ash
The flesh has been burned away

phrases.english: One might think that even once they have become ash
he renders his garments impure?
Therefore the verse says: "them"
they render garments impure,
but once they become ash they do not render garments impure.
Rabbi Shimon says:
they render garments impure,
but once the flesh has been burned away, they do not render garments impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אַף מִשֶּׁנַּעֲשׂוּ אֵפֶר מְטַמֵּא בְּגָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, moving from who becomes טמא to when the טומאה ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, the טומאה lasts until the animals become ash. According to רבי שמעון, it ends once the flesh is burned away.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two views?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a practical case where the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון would rule differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what practical case separates the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון. This question sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views seem to say the same thing: once the animal is burned up, it no longer causes טומאה. The גמרא wants to find the exact middle stage where the two opinions give different results.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the disagreement just presented in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון would rule differently.

steps.title: רבא: a charred lump that is not yet ash
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the two views differ when the animal has become a charred mass but has not yet turned to ash.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The difference between them is when he turned it into a charred lump.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by pointing to the in-between stage, where the animal is charred but not yet ash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the charred stage, the flesh is already burned away, so according to רבי שמעון it no longer causes טומאה. But it is not yet real ash, so according to the תנא קמא it still makes clothes טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: The difference between them is
A charred, scorched lump

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא says the טומאה lasts until the animal becomes real ash. רבי שמעון says it ends once the flesh is burned away. The case that separates them is a charred lump that is not yet ash.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The difference between them is where he turned it into a charred lump.
phrases.notes: The animal is scorched and no longer looks like itself, but it hasn't actually turned to ash yet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דְּשַׁוְּיֵיהּ חָרוֹכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A charred mass that is not yet ash: the תנא קמא says it still makes clothes טמא, and רבי שמעון says it does not.

steps.title: הדרן: closing פרק טבול יום
steps.stepSummary: This is the closing formula for פרק טבול יום.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, טבול יום.
steps.whatsHappening: The פרק ends with the traditional closing line, saying we will come back to learn it again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new argument is made here. This line marks the end of the chapter, and a new פרק begins next.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. The traditional formula for finishing a chapter.
The name of this פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, Tevul Yom

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion.

steps.title: Slaughtering and offering up outside: liable for both
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens. Someone who slaughters a קרבן outside the עזרה and then also offers it up outside is liable for each act separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who slaughters and offers up a קרבן outside is liable for the slaughtering and also liable for the offering up.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה. It rules that a person who does both forbidden acts outside the עזרה, slaughtering and offering up, is liable for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שחוטי חוץ and העלאה בחוץ are two separate איסורים. Doing both to the same animal therefore makes him liable twice. The fact that the animal was already slaughtered outside does not cancel the second liability.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of the משנה text
Slaughtering a קרבן outside the עזרה
Offering up a קרבן on a מזבח
Outside the עזרה of the בית המקדש
Liable to punishment or to bring a קרבן

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core rule of the new פרק. The גמרא will next look for the Torah sources for each separate liability.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One who slaughters and offers up outside
phrases.notes: "Outside" means outside the Temple courtyard, the place where קרבנות must be brought.

phrases.english: is liable for the slaughtering,
and liable for the offering up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק right after the הדרן closing פרק טבול יום
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering and offering up outside the עזרה are two separate liabilities

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי exempts offering up an animal slaughtered outside
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי says that offering up outside is only punishable if the animal was slaughtered inside. If it was slaughtered outside, it was already פסול, so offering it up is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: if he slaughtered inside and offered up outside, he is liable. If he slaughtered outside and offered up outside, he is exempt, because he only offered up something פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי הגלילי disagrees with the first ruling. In his view, offering up outside only counts when the animal was still fit for the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He holds that העלאה בחוץ is a sin only for an animal that could have been brought inside. Slaughtering outside already made the animal פסול. So the later offering up is of a פסול item and carries no liability.

keyTerms.meaning: Inside the עזרה
Exempt; not liable
Invalid; unfit for the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי הגלילי does not say the slaughtering outside is permitted. He only exempts the second act, the offering up.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
If he slaughtered inside and offered up outside, he is liable.
phrases.notes: The words "he is liable" aren't written here, but the משנה takes them for granted.

phrases.english: If he slaughtered outside and offered up outside, he is exempt,
since he offered up only an unfit item.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר: שָׁחַט בִּפְנִים וְהֶעֱלָה בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting opinion to the first ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offering up outside is only punishable if the animal was still fit, meaning it was slaughtered inside

steps.title: The חכמים answer: taking the animal out also makes it פסול
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים point out that even an animal slaughtered inside becomes פסול the moment it is taken outside. By רבי יוסי הגלילי's logic, he should be exempt even in his own case of liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: even one who slaughters inside and offers up outside made it פסול once he took it out.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים challenge רבי יוסי הגלילי's reasoning. They show that it would exempt even the case he himself agrees is liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that leaves the עזרה becomes פסול because of יוצא. So every animal offered up outside is already פסול by the time it is offered. If being פסול exempted a person, no one could ever be liable for העלאה בחוץ.

keyTerms.meaning: He took it out (of the עזרה)
A קרבן that left its proper area and became פסול

phrases.english: They said to him:
Even one who slaughters inside and offers up outside,
once he took it out, he made it unfit.
phrases.notes: The point is that, by your reasoning, he should be exempt too, and you agree he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אַף הַשּׁוֹחֵט בִּפְנִים וּמַעֲלֶה בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי הגלילי's reason that offering up a פסול item is exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every animal taken outside becomes פסול, so his reason would exempt the case he agrees is liable

steps.title: A טמא person eating קדשים is liable whether the food is טהור or טמא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה moves to a parallel topic. A טמא person who eats קדשים is liable whether the קדשים were טמא or טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: A טמא person who ate either טמא קדשים or טהור קדשים is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second case that follows the same pattern of disagreement. This is the view of the חכמים on a טמא person eating קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The איסור of eating קדשים while טמא depends on the person's own טומאה. Whether the food itself was טהור or טמא makes no difference to his liability.

keyTerms.meaning: A ritually impure person
Sanctified food, such as meat of a קרבן
Ritually pure

phrases.english: An impure person who ate

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין קֹדֶשׁ טָמֵא בֵּין קֹדֶשׁ טָהוֹר
phrases.english: whether impure sacred food or pure sacred food
is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַטָּמֵא שֶׁאָכַל בֵּין קֹדֶשׁ טָמֵא בֵּין קֹדֶשׁ טָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, parallel case in the same משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טמא person who eats קדשים is liable regardless of the food's status

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי exempts a טמא person who eats טמא קדשים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי says a טמא person is liable only for eating טהור קדשים. Eating food that was already טמא is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: a טמא person who ate טהור food is liable. A טמא person who ate טמא food is exempt, because he only ate something טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי הגלילי applies the same logic he used for העלאה בחוץ. The איסור applies only when the item eaten was still proper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as he held that offering up a פסול animal is exempt, he holds that eating קדשים that are already טמא is exempt. In his view, the איסור of eating in טומאה applies only to קדשים that are still טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: An impure item

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
An impure person who ate pure food is liable,
and an impure person who ate impure food is exempt,
since he ate only an impure item.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר: טָמֵא שֶׁאָכַל טָהוֹר – חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting opinion to the ruling about the טמא person
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טמא person is liable only for eating קדשים that were טהור

steps.title: The חכמים answer: touching the food already made it טמא
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים argue that a טמא person makes even טהור food טמא as soon as he touches it. By רבי יוסי הגלילי's logic, he should be exempt even in that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: even a טמא person who ate טהור food made it טמא once he touched it.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים use the same kind of reply as before. They show that רבי יוסי הגלילי's reason would exempt even the case he says is liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before eating, the person touches the food, and his touch makes it טמא. So by the time he eats it, the food is always טמא. If eating טמא food exempted him, no טמא person could ever be liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Touched
Made it impure

steps.whatToRemember: In both cases the חכמים use the same argument: the very act of the sin makes the item פסול or טמא. So that cannot be a reason to exempt.

phrases.english: They said to him:
Even an impure person who ate the pure food,
once he touched it, he made it impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אַף טָמֵא שֶׁאָכַל אֶת הַטָּהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוסי הגלילי's reasoning, just as step 14 did
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי הגלילי's reason that eating טמא food is exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Touching the food makes it טמא before it is eaten, so his reason would exempt every case

steps.title: A טהור person eating טמא קדשים is exempt from this איסור
steps.stepSummary: A טהור person who eats טמא קדשים is exempt from the punishment for eating in טומאה. That punishment applies only when the person's body is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A טהור person who ate טמא food is exempt, because one is liable only for the טומאה of his body.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends this section with one more rule. The punishment of eating in טומאה depends on the eater's body, not on the food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כרת for eating קדשים in טומאה is tied to טומאת הגוף, the eater's own impurity. A טהור person who eats טמא food does not get this punishment, even though eating that food is forbidden in another way.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity of the person's body

steps.confusionAlert: "Exempt" here means exempt from כרת or the קרבן for eating in טומאה. It does not mean that eating טמא קדשים is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the חכמים hold that a טמא person is liable even for טמא food: his liability comes from his own body, not from the food.

phrases.english: And a pure person who ate impure food is exempt,
since one is not liable
except for impurity of the body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the opposite case and states the principle behind the liability
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability for eating קדשים in טומאה depends only on the eater's body

steps.title: Offering up outside has both a punishment and a warning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by saying that liability for offering up (העלאה) outside is easy to understand. The Torah writes both the punishment and the warning for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It makes sense that one is liable for offering up outside, because the Torah writes both a punishment and a warning. The punishment comes from ״and he did not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.″ The warning comes from ״Take heed to yourself, lest you offer up your burnt offerings.″
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by stating the easy case, offering up outside, where both parts of the law are clearly written. This sets up the harder question about slaughtering that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To be punished for a sin, the Torah must write a punishment (עונש) and also a warning not to do it (אזהרה). For העלאה בחוץ both are written: the punishment of כרת and the warning ״הִשָּׁמֶר לְךָ פֶּן תַּעֲלֶה״. The word בשלמא, ״granted,″ tells us a contrast is about to come.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה begins here
Granted; it makes sense (sets up a contrast)
He offered up a sacrifice on an altar
The punishment the Torah gives for a sin
The Torah's warning not to do it (a לאו)

steps.confusionAlert: עונש and אזהרה are two separate things. Knowing the punishment is not enough; the Torah must also give a warning before a person can be punished.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Granted, for offering up outside,
a punishment is written and a warning is written.
The punishment, as it is written:
″And he did not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.″
phrases.notes: ויקרא פרק 17. The same section ends with the punishment of כרת.

phrases.english: The warning, as it is written:
″Take heed to yourself, lest you offer up your burnt offerings.″

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא הֶעֱלָה – כְּתִיב עוֹנֶשׁ וּכְתִיב אַזְהָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה, after the משנה's statements in the earlier steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offering up outside has both a written punishment (כרת) and a written warning (השמר פן תעלה).

steps.title: Why the word ״השמר″ counts as a warning
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין quotes רבי אלעזר: whenever the Torah says השמר, פן, or אל, it is a negative commandment. This shows that ״השמר פן תעלה″ is a real warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רבי אבין said in the name of רבי אלעזר: Every place the Torah says ″take heed,″ ″lest,″ or ″do not,″ it is a negative commandment (לא תעשה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the claim from the last step by citing a general rule about how the Torah phrases prohibitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think ״השמר″ is only good advice and not a real prohibition. רבי אלעזר's rule says that השמר, פן, and אל always make a לא תעשה. So the warning for העלאה בחוץ is a true לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: Take heed; be careful
Lest
Do not
A negative commandment

phrases.english: And this is like what Rabbi Avin said
that Rabbi Elazar said:
Every place where it says
″take heed,″ ″lest,″ or ″do not,″
it is nothing other than a negative commandment.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in Step 19 that ״השמר פן תעלה″ is a valid warning.
steps.raayaObject: That ״השמר פן תעלה עולותיך″ counts as a לא תעשה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר's general rule (quoted by רבי אבין) that השמר, פן, and אל always mean a negative commandment

steps.title: Where is the warning for slaughtering outside?
steps.stepSummary: For slaughtering outside, the punishment is written, but where does the Torah give the warning?
steps.simpleTranslation: But for slaughtering outside: granted, the punishment is written, ″and he did not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.″ But from where do we know the warning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the harder case, slaughtering outside, and asks where its warning is written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same section in ויקרא gives כרת for slaughtering outside, so the punishment is clear. But we have not yet found a לאו for slaughtering, and without one a person cannot be punished.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering the animal
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: But slaughtering:
granted the punishment, as it is written:
″And he did not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.″
But the warning, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with Step 19: offering up has both parts written, but slaughtering seems to be missing a warning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source of the אזהרה (לאו) against slaughtering קדשים outside

steps.title: The warning comes from ״And they shall not slaughter anymore″
steps.stepSummary: The warning for slaughtering outside comes from the פסוק ״וְלֹא יִזְבְּחוּ עוֹד″.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: ″And they shall not slaughter anymore.″
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by pointing to a פסוק in the same section that says not to slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after the punishment for slaughtering outside, the Torah says ״וְלֹא יִזְבְּחוּ עוֹד״. The גמרא reads this as the לאו against slaughtering outside.

keyTerms.meaning: And they shall not slaughter anymore

phrases.english: The verse says:
″And they shall not slaughter anymore.″

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The אזהרה for slaughtering outside is ״וְלֹא יִזְבְּחוּ עוֹד״ (ויקרא 17:7).

steps.title: That פסוק is already used by רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that רבי אלעזר uses ״ולא יזבחו עוד את זבחיהם″ to teach that slaughtering to מרקוליס is forbidden, even though that is not its normal way of worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this פסוק is needed for רבי אלעזר's teaching. He said: From where do we know that someone who slaughters an animal to מרקוליס is liable? As it is written, ″And they shall not slaughter anymore their offerings.″ It cannot be teaching worship in the idol's normal way, because that is already written in ″How do they serve.″ So apply it to worship that is not the idol's normal way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer, because the same פסוק is already being used for a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרקוליס was normally worshipped in a different way, not by slaughtering. ״איכה יעבדו″ already forbids worshipping any idol in its normal way. So רבי אלעזר says ״ולא יזבחו″ must be teaching that slaughtering is forbidden for every idol, even when that is not its normal way. If the פסוק is busy with that, it seems it cannot also be the warning for slaughtering outside.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (a different teaching)
An idol that was not normally worshipped by slaughtering
In its normal way of worship
If it is not needed for this matter, apply it to another

phrases.english: But this is needed for the teaching of Rabbi Elazar!
As he said: From where do we know
that one who slaughters an animal to Mercury
is liable?
As it is written: ″And they shall not slaughter anymore
their offerings.″
If it is not needed for the matter of its normal way of worship,
since it is written: ″How do they serve,″
phrases.notes: דברים 12:30. This פסוק already forbids worshipping an idol in its normal way.

phrases.english: apply it to the matter of worship not in its normal way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source given in Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using ״ולא יזבחו עוד″ as the warning for slaughtering outside
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is already used by רבי אלעזר for slaughtering to an idol in an unusual way, so it seems it cannot also teach the warning for slaughtering outside.

steps.title: רבה: read the פסוק two ways
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the פסוק can be read in two ways at once, so it teaches both laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Read it as ″And they shall not slaughter,″ and also read it as ″and not anymore.″
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the challenge by showing that one פסוק can carry both teachings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read as ״ולא יזבחו″, stopping there, the words go back to the earlier פסוקים about slaughtering outside and give their warning. Read as ״ולא עוד″ together with the rest, ״their offerings to the שעירים״, they teach רבי אלעזר's law about idol worship. So there is no conflict.

keyTerms.meaning: Read it as (read the פסוק this way)
And not anymore

steps.whatToRemember: The warning for slaughtering קדשים outside is ״וְלֹא יִזְבְּחוּ״. The same פסוק, read as ״וְלֹא עוֹד אֶת זִבְחֵיהֶם״, also teaches רבי אלעזר's law about idol worship.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
Read it as ″And they shall not slaughter,″
phrases.notes: He means stop right there; this part is the warning against slaughtering outside.

phrases.english: and also read it as ″and not anymore.″
phrases.notes: This reading joins up with ″their offerings to the שעירים″ and teaches the law about idols.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dual reading of the same פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One פסוק can only teach one law, so ״ולא יזבחו עוד″ cannot be both the idol-worship source and the warning for slaughtering outside.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק is read two ways: ״ולא יזבחו″ is the warning for slaughtering outside, and ״ולא עוד״ teaches רבי אלעזר's idol-worship law.

steps.title: The verse is still needed for a teaching about the period of private altars
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that ״ולא יזבחו עוד″ is already used by a ברייתא. The ברייתא begins by saying the earlier verses speak about offerings consecrated and offered while בָּמוֹת were forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the פסוק is still needed for what a ברייתא teaches: Up to this point, the Torah is speaking about sacred offerings that a person consecrated during the time when private altars were forbidden, and offered during the time when private altars were forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is challenging רבה's answer again. It says the פסוק ״ולא יזבחו עוד″ is still busy with another teaching, and it starts quoting the ברייתא that shows this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה showed that the פסוק could carry two lessons at once. Now the גמרא says a ברייתא uses the same words for a separate point about when the offering was consecrated and when it was offered, compared with whether בָּמוֹת were allowed at those times. If the פסוק is needed for that, it may not be free to serve as the warning against slaughtering outside.

keyTerms.meaning: Still / yet: introduces a renewed challenge even after the last answer
Private altars, which were allowed at certain times in history
The period when private altars were forbidden
He consecrated them, making the animals holy as offerings

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not finished here. It is only the first half, and the contrast it is building toward comes in the next lines.

phrases.english: Still, he needs it
phrases.notes: "It" is the פסוק ״וְלֹא יִזְבְּחוּ עוֹד״ that רבה just used for two laws.

phrases.english: for that which was taught in a ברייתא:
Up to here, it is speaking
phrases.notes: "Up to here" means the verses about slaughtering outside that come before ״ולא יזבחו עוד״.

phrases.english: about sacred offerings that one consecrated
at a time when private altars were forbidden
and offered them at a time when private altars were forbidden –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Renews the challenge to step 22 after רבה's answer in step 24, pointing to yet another use of the same פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim (steps 22 and 24) that ״ולא יזבחו עוד″ can be the warning against slaughtering outside
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק already used by a ברייתא for a different teaching cannot simply be taken as the warning. Since this ברייתא uses the פסוק to distinguish times when בָּמוֹת were forbidden, the warning still has no free source.
